A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same representation-dispersion research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original dispersion–perplexity analyses, controlled correctness-slice experiments, model and layer comparisons, and auxiliary-loss training results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds calibration, alternative-metric, distribution-shift, training-trajectory, and squeeze-ablation experiments.

M1.justification: The dispersion statistic, dispersion-gap score, layer-selection rule, and push-away objectives are retained. Appendix B.1.3 adds a regression-based calibration procedure: fit and validate a mapping from dispersion to accuracy using labeled data, then apply it to unseen data. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation coverage with HELLASWAG_CHAT, IF_EVAL, and QUAIL controlled-slice experiments in B.1.4, plus GSM8K in the OLMo training-trajectory study. Multilingual MMLU, WikiText, news, PubMed, MATH, and HumanEval were already represented in v1 and are retained.

E2.justification: B.1.2 adds query-text perplexity as a directly evaluated competing hardness signal on the same MMLU and ARC-Challenge correctness slices. v1 reported dispersion for this application without that comparator. Existing training-baseline and attention-versus-FFN comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 20%/10%/70% calibration/validation/test split with 2-percentage-point calibration increments, validation-selected regressors, and zero-shot evaluation of 30 OLMo-7B checkpoints sampled every 20,000 steps from 120,000 to 700,000. v2 also introduces held-out-split testing, Vendi Score measurement, and a reversed-loss control. Retained experiments largely preserve their settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive tests of held-out generalization and metric robustness (A.4–A.5), calibration and distribution shift (B.1.3–B.1.4), model-selection robustness across training checkpoints (B.2.2), and the effect of deliberately suppressing dispersion (B.4.2). These investigate questions not tested by the corresponding v1 analyses.

E5.justification: The model-selection distance tables gain mean ± standard error reporting: v1 Tables 3–4 become v2 Tables 9–12. Figure 33 also introduces 95% confidence bands. v1 already reported seed-based errors and correlation significance elsewhere; the PDFs do not establish increased run counts for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: New results include calibration MAEs of 1.39, 1.75, and 2.15 percentage points (Table 5), OLMo rank correlations of 0.90 and 0.95, and squeeze perplexity of 101.7 versus baseline 83.0 at 1,000 steps with learning rate 5 × 10^-4 (Table 13). Existing distances also change beyond rounding: Qwen2.5-1.5B Euclidean D–NM changes from 1.54 to 1.4331. Original Tables 1–2 and listed MATH/HumanEval performance scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The dispersion and dispersion-gap definitions, algebraic training objectives, Transformer equations, and uniform-binning algorithm are retained. v2 condenses equations and makes auxiliary-loss notation explicit, but adds no substantive mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the broad claim of predicting unlabeled downstream accuracy with relative difficulty ranking and hard-slice discovery. Model selection is narrowed from reliably identifying better variants to coarse screening within a model family before full evaluation. The conclusion also drops its explicit unlabeled accuracy-estimation claim.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes relative hardness from calibrated accuracy, restricts model screening by family/tokenizer, and explains that calibration requires labeled, model- and domain-specific data. It interprets the perplexity comparison as evidence beyond next-token confidence and the squeeze ablation as causal evidence. Appendix C remains unchanged, including its caution that causality is not definitively established.

D1.justification: v2 documents calibration-batch construction, candidate regression models and validation selection, the OLMo checkpoint schedule and burn-in exclusion, and the squeeze weight λ = 0.1. These provide reproduction details for the additions. Existing hardware disclosures, training hyperparameters, search grids, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Friedman and Dieng's Vendi Score reference. B.4.3 expands the relationship to already-cited supervised contrastive learning and ContraCLM, explicitly positioning the push-away loss as a simplified contrastive/repulsive regularizer rather than an entirely new idea. The remaining cited literature is retained despite bibliography-format changes.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 4; the accuracy-prediction application is retitled as hardness ranking. Selected application passages, interpretability discussion, and the conclusion are rewritten or condensed, and an LLM-usage statement and updated author information appear. Most existing prose and appendix explanations are preserved.

P2.justification: The ICLR format changes the title block, headings, running headers, and main-text layout. Table 1 is reorganized with sample sizes across columns, while v1 Tables 3–4 are split into v2 Tables 9–12. New generalization, metric-comparison, and trajectory figures and several new result tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central diagnostic contribution. v1 inferred unlabeled accuracy prediction from controlled correctness mixtures; v2 narrows that claim, compares against perplexity, and separately evaluates calibration requiring labels on disjoint data. New robustness tests and the reverse-loss intervention address important gaps in the original evidence. Remaining perfect-ranking overstatements, strong causal wording, and the inconsistent Figure 22 caption limit the revision, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidential support and claim precision.
